**Step:** [step-9](../README.md) — Does the mechanism class of the child's BUB1B alleles, checked against sources that share nothing (a structure atlas, mouse phenotypes, expression signatures, cell-line screens, the child's own pharmacogenome, phenotype-specific safety), support each drug direction — and which approved candidates survive all of them?
**Status:** supported  |  **Confidence:** 0.40  |  **Revisions:** 2
**Gene:** —  |  **Path:** e5-pgx

## The claim

P4-25: the child's own genome carries at least one pharmacogenomic result that changes how a shortlisted candidate would be prescribed

**Prediction if true.** PharmCAT plus CPIC over the child's genotypes returns at least one non-normal phenotype for a gene governing a shortlisted drug (SLCO1B1, ABCG2 or CYP2C9 for the statins; CYP3A5 for vincristine; CYP2C9 for valproate; G6PD for chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine)

**What would refute it.** every relevant gene calls a normal phenotype, or too few pharmacogene positions are callable to make a diplotype for any of them

## Evidence

| # | Direction | Strength | Kind | Observation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 209 | supports | 0.35 | measurement | PharmCAT 3.4.0 on the child's callset returns an observed non-normal phenotype for CYP3A5 (poor metaboliser), CYP2C19 (poor/intermediate), CYP2B6 (intermediate) and RYR1 (uncertain malignant-hyperthermia susceptibility); CYP3A5 is in the pre-registered gene list and is the gene of the one paediatric-rhabdomyosarcoma pharmacogenomic study (PMID 38680001) | `docs/iteration4/step-9/methodology/152-is-each-candidate-safe-for-this-child.md` |
| 210 | neutral | 0.70 | measurement | Only 20 of 1,223 distinct PharmCAT definition positions are genotyped (1.6 percent). Every gene with a guideline for a shortlisted drug - SLCO1B1 (all three statins, CPIC level A), G6PD (chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine), UGT1A1 (irinotecan) - is a no call; their phenotypes exist only under --absent-to-ref, which PharmCAT labels DANGEROUS | `docs/iteration4/step-9/methodology/152-is-each-candidate-safe-for-this-child.md` |
| 211 | neutral | 0.40 | measurement | CYP3A5 poor metabolism is the majority phenotype in European-ancestry populations and CPIC has no vincristine-CYP3A5 guideline, so the call is non-normal by name and common by frequency | `docs/iteration4/step-9/methodology/152-is-each-candidate-safe-for-this-child.md` |

The weighing is a transparent heuristic for triage, not a calibrated posterior: the strengths are human judgments, and rows drawn from the same underlying data are not independent the way the sum treats them.

**The committed confidence differs from the suggestion by -0.27.** The reasoning below is why.
